verdict.rationale: AWS documents a single CLI that controls multiple services, can surface documentation inline, and covers functionality equivalent to the console. There is also a dedicated API Reference for a non-flagship service (Cost Explorer) and a structured llms.txt index of service documentation. However, nothing in the evidence shows that every service has a consistent API/CLI reference, and no machine-readable OpenAPI spec was found. missing for 10: evidence of per-service CLI command reference across the whole platform, evidence of consistent API reference coverage beyond a few services, independent corroboration of reference-doc consistency.

support.subject: As a developer, every service has a real reference — consistent API/CLI reference docs across the platform, not just the flagship services

citations.quote: With just one tool to download and configure, you can control multiple AWS services from the command line and automate them through scripts.
The AWS CLI v2 can prompt you with commands, parameters, resources, documentation, and more when running an 'aws' command.
You can use the Cost Explorer API to programmatically query your cost and usage data.
